prerequisites: Mechanics: content of the Statics lecture
Mathematics: Trigonometry, Algebra, Basics of Differential and Integral Calculus, simple Differential Equations
Materials Science: Material types, Material properties

learning_outcomes.text: Students can name the terms mechanical stress and strain and explain the differences.
Students can name and explain the material laws and properties necessary for strength of materials.
Students can name various strength hypotheses and explain their application.
Students can name and present the basic types of loading (tension, compression and temperature change in rods, bending, shear and torsion).
Students can describe the importance of strength of materials within engineering using practical examples.
Students can perform stress analysis for rods and beams using the methods of strength of materials and explain the significance of equivalent stresses for superimposed loads.
Students can differentiate the areas of application for strength hypotheses.
Students can describe stress and strain states under multi-axial loading conditions and calculate stresses and strains in different spatial directions.
Students can calculate principal and equivalent stresses and select suitable strength hypotheses.
Students can distinguish between and calculate statically determinate and indeterminate systems.
Students can calculate the deformation and stress state of components under basic load types.
Students can select and calculate the appropriate equivalent stress for superimposed loads.
Students can assess and evaluate the limitations of strength calculations using elementary methods.
Students can prepare and document engineering problems, solutions, and solution paths.
Students are able to independently learn to calculate more complex problems using advanced literature.
Students can prepare, present, and discuss results of selected analyses and calculations in groups.

syllabus_topics: Tensile and compressive stress in rods
Selected specific topics in strength of materials
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is a written exam. The duration and scope of the exam are as specified in the currently valid study regulations.
